# Files, CSV and JSON


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Read text with `•nget`, parse it with `•csv` or `•json`, and calculate.
`•tocsv` and `•tojson` produce text, which `•nput` writes to a file.

``` text
sales←•csv •nget "sales.csv"
totals←+/¨sales
"totals.json" •nput •tojson totals
```

Options go on the left as a keyed vector, and the data goes on the
right. Option names are case-insensitive.

## Files

``` bpl
]help •nget
```

`•nget path` reads a UTF-8 text file. `•nget "-"` reads the rest of
standard input. A path that starts with `./` or `../` is relative to the
file holding the code, as for [`•load`](#load).

`X •nget path` takes options on the left: `binary` (`1` reads a vector
of byte values) and `encoding` (`"UTF-8"`). [Files](data.ipynb#files)
covers bytes and options.

Errors: `VALUE` for missing files, invalid UTF-8, other file errors and
standard input that the frontend doesn’t provide; `DOMAIN` for invalid
options.

``` bpl
]help •nput
```

`path •nput data` writes `data` to a new file. It returns the number of
bytes written. Text is written as UTF-8. An array of numbers is written
as bytes, each from 0 to 255, in ravel order. A path that starts with
`./` or `../` is relative to the file holding the code, as for
[`•load`](#load).

`X •nput data` takes options on the left: `path`, `overwrite` (`1`
replaces an existing file) and `encoding` (`"UTF-8"`, for text). Plain
text on the left is the path. [Files](data.ipynb#files) covers bytes and
options.

Errors: `VALUE` for an existing file without `overwrite`, and for other
file errors; `DOMAIN` for invalid options or byte values.

``` bpl
text←•nget "sales.csv"
"copy.csv" •nput text
["path":"copy.csv" "overwrite":1] •nput text
```

Directories must already exist. Binary reads return exact integers in
`0…255`. `•nput` writes an array of numbers as bytes, each an integer in
that range. It checks the data before opening the file.

``` bpl
bytes←["binary":1] •nget "image.bin"
"copy.bin" •nput bytes
"UTF-8" •ucs bytes           ⍝ decode UTF-8 when appropriate
bytes-256ₓ×bytes≥128ₓ         ⍝ signed-byte interpretation
```

## Numeric input

``` bpl
]help •vfi
```

`•vfi text` returns two vectors, `[valid numbers]`, for the
whitespace-separated fields of `text`. An invalid field has the flag
`0ₓ` and the value `0`. Fields are parsed as numbers, never executed.

`separators •vfi text` splits on each character in `separators` instead.
It trims whitespace around fields. An empty field is a valid `0`.
[Numeric input](data.ipynb#numeric-input) covers it.

Errors: `DOMAIN` when either argument is not text.

Invalid fields have flag `0ₓ` and value `0`. Valid fields have flag
`1ₓ`:

``` bpl
[valid nums]←•vfi "12 nope -3 1.5"
valid
nums
valid#nums
```

    [1 0 1 1]ₓ

    12 0 ¯3 1.5

    12 ¯3 1.5

A number written plainly, such as `2` or `1.5`, is approximate. A number
written with an `x` suffix, such as `3x`, or as a rational, such as
`1r4`, is exact. `•vfi` also accepts complex numbers written with `j` or
`J`, `∞`, `inf`, `infinity`, ASCII signs and signed exponents. `nan`
gives `$n`. An invalid field gives the number `0` with the flag `0ₓ`.

The numbers all become approximate when one of them is approximate and a
float can represent every one exactly. Otherwise each number keeps its
kind. The `0` from an invalid field doesn’t count as approximate.

``` bpl
1⊃•vfi "2 3x 1r4 1j-2 -1e-3 ∞"
```

    2 3ₓ 1ᵣ4 1ⱼ¯2 ¯0.001 ∞

`separators •vfi text` splits on any supplied character and trims
surrounding whitespace. Empty fields are valid zero. Internal whitespace
remains part of the field.

``` bpl
',' •vfi "3.9,2.4,,76,"
'⋄' •vfi "1 ⋄ 2 3 ⋄ 4"
```

    (1ₓ 1ₓ 1ₓ 1ₓ 1ₓ ⋄ 3.9 2.4 0 76 0)

    (1ₓ 0ₓ 1ₓ ⋄ 1 0 4)

Empty input returns two empty vectors. With no separator characters
(`""` on the left), nonempty input is one field. DOMAIN: either argument
is not character text.

## JSON

``` bpl
]help •json
```

`•json text` parses JSON. Objects become keyed vectors. Arrays become
vectors. Strings become character vectors. Integers stay exact. `true`
and `false` become `$t` and `$f`.

`["fill":v] •json text` replaces `null` with `v`. The default is NaN. An
integer array with a `null` stays exact. [JSON](data.ipynb#json) covers
the conversions.

Errors: `DOMAIN` for malformed JSON, with its line and column.

Nested structure is kept:

``` bpl
person←•json "{""name"":""Ann"",""scores"":[10,20]}"
person.name
person.scores
```

    Ann

    [10 20]ₓ

``` bpl
]help •tojson
```

`•tojson Y` returns JSON text. Keyed axes become objects. Unkeyed axes
become arrays. Character vectors become strings. Keyed entries that hold
functions are left out.

NaN exports as `null`. `["fill":v] •tojson Y` also writes `v` as `null`.
[JSON](data.ipynb#json) covers the conversions.

Errors: `DOMAIN` for an infinity that isn’t `fill`, out-of-range floats,
nonintegral rationals, complex numbers and other functions.

`"f.json" •nput •tojson Y` writes JSON to a file. Scalar arrays export
their contents. Axis names and empty-array prototypes are left out:

``` bpl
•tojson ["name":"Ann" "scores":[10 20]ₓ]
•tojson [1 2 ⋄ 3 4]ₓ
•tojson •json "{}"
```

    {"name":"Ann","scores":[10,20]}

    [[1,2],[3,4]]

    {}

JSON integers are exact. Numbers with a decimal point or an exponent are
approximate. An array’s numbers combine by the rule in [Numeric
input](#numeric-input). `true` and `false` read as `$t` and `$f`.
`•tojson` writes Booleans back as `true` and `false`:

``` bpl
•json "[9223372036854775809,1.5,true,false]"
•tojson •json "[true,false]"
```

    9223372036854775809ₓ 1.5 $t $f

    [true,false]

`fill` replaces `null` on import. The default is NaN. On export, NaN and
the `fill` value become `null`:

``` bpl
•json "[1,null,3]"
["fill":¯1ₓ] •json "[1,null,3]"
["fill":∞] •tojson 1ₓ ∞ 3ₓ
```

    [1 $n 3]ₓ

    [1 ¯1 3]ₓ

    [1,null,3]

Duplicate object members keep the last value.

## CSV

``` bpl
]help •csv
```

`•csv text` parses CSV into a vector of columns. Headers become keys.
Numeric columns become numbers. Missing numeric cells become NaN. An
integer column with missing cells stays exact. Missing text cells become
`""`.

`X •csv text` takes options on the left: `header`, `separator`,
`quotechar`, `doublequote`, `escapechar`, `decimal`, `thousands`,
`trim`, `fill`, `text_columns`, `numeric_columns` and `missing`.
[CSV](data.ipynb#csv) describes them.

Errors: `DOMAIN` for invalid options or duplicate headers; `LENGTH` for
unequal record widths.

Each numeric column uses compact integer or float storage where
possible:

``` bpl
nl←•ucs 10
text←"price,qty",nl,"10.5,2",nl,"20.0,4"
T←•csv text
T
T.qty
+/¨T
```

    ["price":[10.5 20] "qty":[2 4]ₓ]

    [2 4]ₓ

    ["price":30.5 "qty":6ₓ]

``` bpl
]help •tocsv
```

`•tocsv T` returns CSV text for a vector of columns. Keys supply the
header. Column lengths must agree.

`X •tocsv T` takes options on the left: `header`, `separator`,
`quotechar`, `doublequote`, `escapechar`, `decimal`, `thousands`,
`trim`, `fill`, `forcequotes` and `lineending`. NaN writes as an empty
cell, and so does the exact value given as `fill`. `"forcequotes":2`
quotes every field. [CSV](data.ipynb#csv) describes the options.

Errors: `DOMAIN` for nonintegral rationals, complex numbers, functions
or nested cells; `LENGTH` for unequal columns.

`"f.csv" •nput •tocsv T` writes CSV to a file. Unkeyed input writes the
data without a header. Parsing the text restores the columns:

``` bpl
T←["price":[10.5 20] "qty":[2ₓ 4ₓ]]
•csv •tocsv T
```

    ["price":[10.5 20] "qty":[2 4]ₓ]

### CSV options

``` bpl
nl←•ucs 10
text←"price;qty",nl,"10,5;2",nl,"20,0;4"
opts←["separator":';' "decimal":',']
T←opts •csv text
T
csv←opts •tocsv T
opts •csv csv
```

    ["price":[10.5 20] "qty":[2 4]ₓ]

    ["price":[10.5 20] "qty":[2 4]ₓ]

Column selectors are names or positions, counting from 0. A character
vector names one column. Use a vector for several selectors.

``` bpl
text←"id,qty",(•ucs 10),"00123,5"
T←["text_columns":"id"] •csv text
T.id
```

    ["00123"]

Separator, quote and escape must be distinct ASCII characters other than
CR, LF or NUL. Fields support Unicode, doubled quotes and embedded
newlines. Import accepts LF, CRLF and CR record endings. Export with
`escapechar` quotes every field and doubles literal escape characters.
With quoting disabled, export errors if a field requires quoting.

### Numbers and missing cells

Inference examines a whole column, ignoring missing cells. Integer
fields produce exact numbers. Decimal/scientific notation produces
floats. A column containing other text stays text. Quoted numbers
participate in inference too.

``` bpl
nl←•ucs 10
T←•csv "count,label",nl,"2,001",nl,"3,yes"
T.count
T.label
```

    [2 3]ₓ

    "001" "yes"

A column of integers uses `i64` storage when every value fits. Integers
beyond `i64` stay exact. A value with a decimal point or an exponent is
approximate. A column’s numbers combine by the rule in [Numeric
input](#numeric-input).

Missing numeric cells become NaN, written `$n`. A missing cell never
makes a column float. An integer column with a gap stays exact, in
integer storage. Missing text cells become `""`. Entirely missing
columns are text unless forced numeric.

``` bpl
nl←•ucs 10
T←•csv "price,qty",nl,"10.5,2",nl,",4"
T.price
T.qty
```

    10.5 $n

    [2 4]ₓ

Configure extra missing markers and numeric fill explicitly.

``` bpl
text←"qty",(•ucs 10),"NA",(•ucs 10),"4"
["missing":"NA" "fill":¯1ₓ] •csv text
```

    ["qty":[¯1 4]ₓ]

Export uses `-` for negative numbers, decimal/scientific float spelling
and plain exact integers. Infinity writes as `inf` or `-inf`. Set `fill`
to export a chosen numeric sentinel as an empty field. Nonintegral
rationals, complex numbers, functions and nested nonstring cells give
DOMAIN.

Empty input returns an empty unkeyed vector. Header-only input returns
keyed empty columns. Empty header names are allowed. Duplicate header
names give DOMAIN. Unequal record widths or column lengths give LENGTH.
Invalid forced numeric fields report their row and column.
